summary: Smoke-tested the refactored TROA backend (server.py split into routes/*). 17/17 pytest backend tests passed via the public preview URL. All public GETs (committee, amenities, gallery, events, health) return 200; auth-protected endpoints (feedback, invoices, users, membership-GET, invoices/{id}/pdf, invoices/pending/count) correctly return 401; membership POST works (200) with correct payload schema (firstName/lastName/villaNo); WebSocket /api/chat/ws/{group_id} endpoint is reachable. Frontend pages (/, /committee, /amenities, /events, /gallery, /about, /contact, /login) all load 200 with no JS pageerrors. One latent bug found in routes/membership.py: notification side-effects use stale attribute names from the old monolith.

minor.issue: Membership application is created (200 OK), but the email + push notification side-effects silently fail. Backend log: `'MembershipApplication' object has no attribute 'name'`. routes/membership.py references app_obj.name / app_obj.villa_no, but models.MembershipApplication exposes firstName / lastName / villaNo. The exceptions are swallowed by inner try/except so the API still succeeds, but admins/managers receive NO notification of new applications.

integration_issues.issue: GSI logs '[GSI_LOGGER]: The given origin is not allowed for the given client ID.' on the preview URL. Expected for non-prod origin; not a refactoring regression. Email/password login should still work.

action_items: Fix routes/membership.py: replace app_obj.name with f"{app_obj.firstName} {app_obj.lastName or ''}".strip(), app_obj.villa_no -> app_obj.villaNo. Also for `applicant_phone=app_obj.phone` (this one is correct, phone exists). The push notification body and admin email use the same wrong attribute names. After fix, /api/membership should no longer emit AttributeError in backend logs and admin notifications will actually be sent.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/membership.py uses stale attribute names from the pre-refactor monolith (name, villa_no) that do not exist on the MembershipApplication pydantic model (which uses firstName/lastName/villaNo). Inner try/except swallows the AttributeError so it appears to work but notifications are silently dropped.
routes/gallery.py POST endpoint has no auth guard (any caller can create gallery images). Compare with committee/amenities which require admin. Likely a pre-existing issue but worth confirming.

Cache-Control middleware in server.py: response Cache-Control header observed on /api/committee was 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' instead of the expected 'public, max-age=300, ...'. Likely an ingress/CDN override at the preview proxy — functional behavior unaffected but worth verifying in production.
server.py uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') hooks. Consider migrating to lifespan handlers (FastAPI >=0.93).
test_credentials: No working password known. Sessions can be injected via Mongo as documented in /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
seed_data_creation: Created 2 test membership applications with firstName=TEST_Applicant_* and villaNo=TEST-001 in db.membership_applications. Safe to delete by prefix.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_23 confirms refactoring is functionally clean for unauthenticated flows. Authenticated CRUD (invoices, bookings, payments, chat WS auth, push) was NOT exercised in this iteration because no working password is available — inject a session token to extend coverage. The only regression-class bug found is the membership notification AttributeError; the API still responds 200 so end users won't notice but admins miss notifications.
rca of the issue: When server.py was split, routes/membership.py was extracted but the notification side-effect block still references attributes from a pre-refactor model variant (.name, .villa_no). The current models.MembershipApplication / MembershipApplicationCreate define firstName, lastName, villaNo. Because the calls are wrapped in `try/except Exception as email_error: logger.error(...)`, the AttributeError is logged but never surfaces to the API client, so the POST returns 200 with the application created in DB while no admin gets notified.
